evaluatedLibraries.name: Electron safeStorage
evaluatedLibraries.maintenance: Active (Core Electron API, maintained by Electron team)
evaluatedLibraries.sizeLimit: No artificial limit (tested up to 1 MB+ seamlessly)
evaluatedLibraries.nativeDependency: None (built into Electron binary, zero ABI rebuild issues)
evaluatedLibraries.userIsolation: Enforced via Windows DPAPI Master Key (tied to SID + logon password)
evaluatedLibraries.systemUiPollution: Zero (ciphertext stored privately in app DB/file, invisible in Control Panel)
evaluatedLibraries.accountWipe: 100% clean (deleting DB/file leaves zero orphaned credentials in OS)

evaluatedLibraries.name: keytar (github.com/atom/node-keytar)
evaluatedLibraries.maintenance: Archived by GitHub in 2022. No further updates.
evaluatedLibraries.mechanism: Native C++ binding to Advapi32.dll (Windows Credential Manager)
evaluatedLibraries.nativeDependency: Heavy (native C++ node-gyp module, frequently breaks on Node/Electron ABI upgrades)
evaluatedLibraries.systemUiPollution: High (every key appears in Control Panel > Credential Manager)
evaluatedLibraries.accountWipe: Error-prone (requires manual enumeration; orphaned keys persist if target name is lost)

evaluatedLibraries.name: Windows Credential Manager (Native Win32)
evaluatedLibraries.sizeLimit: Hard limit 2560 bytes (CRED_MAX_GENERIC_CREDENTIAL_BLOB_SIZE). Win32 Error 1783 on exceed.
evaluatedLibraries.nativeDependency: Requires custom native addon or P/Invoke wrapper

vsCodeReference.precedent: VS Code previously used keytar, but deprecated and completely removed it in 2022 (VS Code PR #167098) in favor of Electron safeStorage.
vsCodeReference.rationale: Eliminated native build failures across ABI versions, removed Credential Manager size boundaries, and prevented OS credential clutter.
